newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-RUN OF BIRDIES KEEPS GOOSEN IN FRONT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RUN OF BIRDIES KEEPS GOOSEN IN FRONT.

text.p: South African Retief Goosen collected four successive birdies after the turn to help him take a three-stroke lead into Sunday's final round of the rain-affected French Open.
Goosen had gone into the morning's third round with a four-stroke lead but dropped strokes going out to allow the field to move within two shots of him.
However, he surged away again with his birdie burst before Martin Gates, his playing-partner, cut his lead to three strokes when the Englishman also excelled on back nine.
A two-under-par 70 by Goosen took him to 15-under-par 201, with Gates shooting 69 for 204. Sweden's Robert Karlsson moved up to third a further stroke back.
Tournament favourite Colin Montgomerie was eight shots off the pace.

"The couple of sixes I made on the front nine knocked me back," said Goosen, "but I then played really well for my good run. It's very tiring being on top and I've been nervous. But I know I have to go out and do it all again."

Spain's Diego Borrego made the European Tour's second albatross of the year, coincidentally on the French National's 'Albatross' course, when his three-iron second shot found the cup at the 530-yard par-five third hole. He finished eight off the lead.
